newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says EMU could be good for American economy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says EMU could be good for American economy.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott said on Tuesday that European economic and monetary union could be good for the American economy.

"...we have no doubt that an EMU that cements an open single market and that sparks economic growth in Europe will be good for the American economy," he told a U.S.-European Union conference at the State Department.
Talbott added: "If the EU emerges from this bold initiative able to play an even more active and constructive role on the world stage, that will be good for America too."

In his speech, the deputy secretary also noted that some in Europe "resist vehemently the idea that any nations to the east of what might be called 'traditional Europe' can ever be part of a larger, twenty-first century Europe."
Citing NATO member Turkey specifically, he said "we believe that view is quite wrong and potentially quite dangerous."
He noted that Turkey has been part of the European system since the 16th century and said while Turkey is separated from most of Europe by water, "so is all of the United Kingdom."
Talbott also stressed the importance of not permitting a religious divide among "Catholic, Orthodox and Islamic parts of Europe."
He said the United States has an "ulterior motive" for pressing expansion of NATO into the former communist states of central and eastern Europe.

"We hope that the enlargement of NATO, of which we are a member, will contribute to the conditions for the enlargement of the EU, of which we are not a member but in which we have such a profound -- I'd even say vital -- interest," he said.
